tags: why does my dog ignore me outside
script: Inside the house, your dog hears a treat bag from three rooms away. Outside, they somehow can't hear you at all. It feels like selective hearing, and honestly, in a way it is, but it's not about disrespect. Outdoors, the world is filled with smells, sounds and movement that are far more interesting than your voice, and a dog's nose is far more sensitive than ours. When they're locked onto a scent, their brain is simply busy. Another common reason is training that happened only in quiet places. Dogs don't automatically generalize, so a recall that works in the living room may not mean anything in the park until it's practiced there. Calling and then ending the fun, like clipping on the leash and going home, can also teach them that coming to you is a bad deal. To fix it, practice in gradually busier places, use high-value treats, and make coming back to you the best part of the walk. Use a long line for safety while you build the habit. Over time, your voice can win against even the best smell.
